findings.additional_reduction_feasibility: Potentially avoid a second canonical pass only where the exact same bytes are already produced and consumed in one construction/validation operation; profile supports high cumulative cost but does not prove identical-object duplicate work for every call.
findings.boundary: Repeated canonical serialization/hash for content references
findings.concrete_call_path: fixture_materialization._ref -> run_contracts.content_ref -> _canonical(json validation + full canonical JSON encode) -> SHA256; content_ref/_require_ref_match and _document_size are separate serialization boundaries.
required_invariants: digest must match the current canonical value at the ref boundary
no persistent cache keyed only by object identity or mutable value
retain bounded depth/node/size and exact JSON type validation
reuse only immutable/freshly owned canonical bytes or recompute after mutation

findings.additional_reduction_feasibility: Only conditionally. Preserve public validator independence. A private internal path could skip a second tree copy only when ownership is proven local and the value cannot escape or be mutated by the caller; current pstats alone does not prove that condition.
findings.boundary: Defensive copies returned by large-document validators
findings.concrete_call_path: Public validators validate nested documents and return deepcopy copies; setup workflow repeatedly crosses these validation/ownership boundaries.
required_invariants: returned documents remain independent from input and other calls
no shared mutable nested dict/list across validators or API results
all validation still runs on each value unless an immutable snapshot with freshness proof is introduced

findings.additional_reduction_feasibility: Limited without changing mutability semantics. An immutable cache representation may reduce recursive copies but requires decode cost and must retain caller isolation; likely lower priority than canonicalization and large validator copies.
findings.boundary: Transaction-scoped checked-read cache copy on store and replay
findings.concrete_call_path: read_checks.checked_read wraps 1337 calls; within a transaction it stores an independent copy of results and returns independent copies on cache hits. _copy recursively traverses dict/list/tuple result trees.
required_invariants: cache remains limited to the same DB transaction/scope
transaction-external reads must still observe current committed state
returned mutable trees cannot alias the cache or another caller

llm_integration.note: This profile is setup-only with 60 fixed CI entries and two candidate receipts. It is not representative evidence for fixed 400/800-entry LLM integration; neither timing nor call counts are extrapolated.
llm_integration.source_hypothesis: If the LLM path repeatedly builds and revalidates similarly nested material/ref documents, canonical reference serialization and defensive result copies may scale with its larger collections. The profile does not establish that these exact callers dominate LLM runtime; a separate same-scope LLM profile would be required for attribution.
